title: Dominic and the Letter
premise: In 1847, apprentice clockmaker Rosalind Pemberton is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a sealed letter hidden in its case — written by Dominic Vasseur, a dying clerk who confesses that the Pemberton family name has been forged onto documents implicating them in a smuggling ring they never joined. With Dominic's granddaughter as her reluctant ally, Rosalind must carry the true evidence past three river checkpoints before the spring ice breaks and the conspirators' ship — and their last chance to intercept it — slips away. She succeeds at terrible cost: Dominic dies before seeing his name cleared, but the family adopts Rosalind into their household, giving the orphaned clockmaker the belonging she never measured for herself.
about_author: Bram Almeida is a former museum conservator who spent a decade restoring maritime instruments along northern rivers. This is a second novel drawn from archival letters about forged shipping manifests.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Things
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Summoned to the observatory, she repairs the master clock while cataloguing everything she owns in her head — the habit of an orphan who measures life by what can be carried. She notices a loose panel in the clock case but leaves it untouched. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Case Kept
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Returning at night to finish the escapement, she opens the panel and finds Dominic Vasseur's sealed letter naming the Pembertons in a smuggling plot — and begging whoever finds it to deliver the real evidence before the ice breaks. Emotional beat: dread displacing curiosity.

chapters.title: A Name She Never Chose
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She investigates the Pembertons, expecting villains, and instead finds a warm, grieving household — and Dominic himself, bedridden, who confirms the forgery and begs her help. His granddaughter Marguerite distrusts her. Emotional beat: the shock of kindness from strangers tied to danger.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One River
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The old clerk maps the route: the customs house, the ferry toll, the garrison bridge — each held by a man on the conspirators' payroll. He teaches Rosalind how clerks hide papers inside instrument cases. Emotional beat: urgency sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Terms
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Suspicious of the apprentice, Marguerite tests her, then offers a bargain: help smuggle the evidence and share the risk, or leave and be reported. Rosalind stays. Emotional beat: wary alliance becoming something like trust.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First checkpoint: she hides the letter inside a repaired barometer she is legitimately delivering, but a suspicious inspector demands it be opened. Marguerite creates a diversion; the seal holds by seconds. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into exhilaration.

chapters.title: Ice Groaning
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Delayed by a storm, they shelter with a ferrymaster who knew Dominic, learning the conspirators have discovered the letter is missing and are searching travelers. The river ice begins to crack early. Emotional beat: the ticking clock made literal.

chapters.title: The Toll of Passage
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Second checkpoint: the ferry toll, where the corrupt collector recognizes Marguerite's surname. She pays with a lie about her grandfather's debts, trading dignity for passage. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into courage.

chapters.title: The Bridge Before the Break
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Climax. At the garrison bridge, the third checkpoint, the conspirators' agent waits with soldiers. Rosalind surrenders a decoy case while the real evidence crosses hidden in the master clock's own pendulum bob, which she carries openly as a tradeswoman. The ice breaks behind them. Emotional beat: sacrifice of safety for truth.

chapters.title: Set in Motion
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The evidence reaches the magistrate; the ring collapses and the Pemberton name is cleared, though Dominic dies the night before news arrives. The family asks Rosalind to stay — not as servant, but as daughter and clockmaker of the house. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as belonging.
